blocks.heading: Bounded Evidence Coverage
blocks.text: The proposal's reliance on averaged energy conditions is bounded by the finding that pointwise energy conditions are systematically violated by quantum fields, which necessitates weaker statements such as quantum energy inequalities or averaged energy conditions for broader validity. This supports the design choice to replace pointwise NEC or SEC assumptions with AANEC, but it does not prove that AANEC alone implies the additional explicit averaged null-convergence condition required by the theorem. Astrophysical context is supplied by the observation that the lower edge of the black hole mass gap is dictated by near-final core mass and is robust against variations in metallicity, internal mixing, and stellar wind mass loss. This anchors the mass-gap discussion in stellar-physics mechanisms rather than treating the gap as a direct prediction of the formal theorem.

blocks.heading: Formal Unknowns and Counterexample Limits
blocks.text: Two formal gaps prevent release of any theorem claim. The Misner-Sharp compactness parameter C lacks a supplied mathematical definition, so compactness thresholds and mass scales cannot be computed. The explicit averaged null-convergence condition A5 likewise lacks a formal mathematical form, so candidate witnesses cannot be tested against it. Counterexample analysis therefore remains a boundary case rather than a completed result: a proposed witness is a static, spherically symmetric, regular metric with isotropic pressure and high compactness satisfying AANEC, but its status under A5 and under the stability predicate is unknown. Because the counterexample must satisfy all assumptions, its validity cannot be decided until A5 and C are formally specified.

blocks.heading: Release Criteria for Future Claims
blocks.text: Before any formal claim is released, human review must confirm the following: first, supply the mathematical definition of Misner-Sharp compactness C and its relation to the model-dependent threshold; second, supply the mathematical form of the explicit averaged null-convergence condition A5 and verify whether it is independent of AANEC; third, audit the proposed counterexample witnesses to determine whether they satisfy A5 and the stability predicate or instead violate an assumption; fourth, confirm that all empirical mass-gap statements remain separated from the formal theorem and are treated only as astrophysical consistency constraints.

claim_provenance.statement: Pointwise energy conditions are systematically violated by quantum fields, necessitating the use of weaker statements such as quantum energy inequalities or averaged energy conditions for broader validity.
The location of the lower edge of the black hole mass gap is dictated by the near-final core mass, which sets the resulting black hole mass.
The Misner-Sharp compactness parameter C has no supplied mathematical definition, so thresholds and mass scales cannot be computed.
The explicit averaged null-convergence condition A5 has no supplied mathematical form, so candidate witnesses cannot be tested against it.
The proposed counterexample witness remains a boundary case because its status under A5 and the stability predicate is unknown until those conditions are formally specified.
Human review must confirm the definitions of C and A5, audit the counterexample witnesses, and verify separation of formal and empirical claims before any theorem claim is released.
